body:
> I tested it using GDScript and it works fine, but it doesn't works when using C#

Can you please share the GDScript project you used to test this? I ported your C# project to GDScript and I'm getting the same error (`CANT_CREATE`).

> What I expect to, is to the garbage collector to properly dispose the peer and connection after setting `Multiplayer.MultiplayerPeer = null`

That's not how the .NET garbage collector works. If the peer was only referenced by `Multiplayer.MultiplayerPeer` then setting it to `null` means there are no more references and the garbage collector **MAY** release it. However, there's no guarantee the C# object will ever be released, or that the `Dispose()` method will be called at all. If you want to make sure the `Dispose()` method is called, then you have to call it yourself.

That said, I think this is unrelated to `Dispose()` or the garbage collector, since I was able to reproduce in GDScript, but it does sound like the documentation about this could be improved.

> Can you please share the GDScript project you used to test this? I ported your C# project to GDScript and I'm getting the same error (CANT_CREATE).

I don't know what to tell you, I just created a project following the **Steps to reproduce** I stated before using GDScript in the same editor version, but I don't get an error. I also checked if the port was claimed using the `netstat` command on Windows 10, and seeing if the port was on the list, I call it inside the ```_ready()``` function using OS.execute, like this:
``` gdscript

	var output = []
	
	create_game() # Returns OK
	remove_multiplayer_peer()
	OS.execute("CMD.exe", ["/C","netstat","-ano", "|", "findstr", ":"+str(PORT)], output);
	print(output)
	output.clear()
	
	create_game() # Returns OK
	OS.execute("CMD.exe", ["/C","netstat","-ano", "|", "findstr", ":"+str(PORT)], output);
	print(output)
	output.clear()
```
The first print call prints an empty string, showing that  ```remove_multiplayer_peer()``` works, and the second one shows that the port is being held by an application with a process ID, while the app is running, if we open the resource monitor on windows and search for this ID, we will see the name of the godot instance.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6eab8cd-8b24-43fd-a12d-fea1c1a2dc01)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7199c939-dded-4035-abce-b749e728fb18)

Trying the same trickery but using C# yields:

```c#
        var output = new Godot.Collections.Array();
        CreateGame(); // Returns Error.OK
        RemoveMultiplayerPeer();
        OS.Execute("CMD.exe", new string[]{"/C", "netstat", "-ano", "|", "findstr", ":"+port.ToString()}, output);
        Debug.WriteLine(output);
        output.Clear();

        CreateGame();  // Returns Error.CANT_CREATE
        OS.Execute("CMD.exe", new string[]{"/C", "netstat", "-ano", "|", "findstr", ":"+port.ToString()}, output);
        Debug.WriteLine(output);
        output.Clear();
```

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/81e2579c-e856-4a86-888a-b203e0c3a329)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/175d30b2-49ea-47bb-8c71-540a255c8c7e)

As you can see, calling `RemoveMultiplayerPeer()` doesn't free the port.

Anyways here is the GDScript version:
[gdscript_enet_host_server_test.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18793535/gdscript_enet_host_server_test.zip)

Moving on,

> That's not how the .NET garbage collector works. If the peer was only referenced by Multiplayer.MultiplayerPeer then setting it to null means there are no more references and the garbage collector MAY release it. However, there's no guarantee the C# object will ever be released, or that the Dispose() method will be called at all. If you want to make sure the Dispose() method is called, then you have to call it yourself.

It is stated in the [RefCounted](https://docs.godotengine.org/es/4.x/classes/class_refcounted.html) documentation that in C#, the Garbage Collector

> will free reference-counted objects that are no longer in use

If this is not always the case, then that line should be changed to reflect reality.

Anyways, I tried calling `ENetMultiplayerPeer.Dispose()` and `ENetConnection.Dispose()` before, neither of them free the port, also tried with `ENetMultiplayerPeer.Close()`, no luck either, the only one that seems to work is `ENetConnection.Destroy()`, I though that this was the intended way to terminate networking, thats why I [commented](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-docs-user-notes/discussions/57#discussioncomment-12188866) on the [High-Level multiplayer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/networking/high_level_multiplayer.html) documentation about using `ENetConnection.Destroy()` because it wasn't mentioned in the docs, I was told that this seemed to be a bug, thats why I opened an issue. Tbh, if there is no problem with Dispose(), then I don't know whats happening here, I hope someone smarter will help.

Well I tried to implement these fixes in a project of mine, turns out they don't work, looking around I discover that the only difference with the MRP is that I was setting the compression method on the host using `peer.Host.Compress()` after creating the server, when manually setting the host compression , neither `Dispose()` or `Close()` works, only the original workaround I found of manually calling `Destroy()` on the Host works.
I commented out the Compress() call and both `Dispose()` and `Close()` fixes work, weird.

I tested this on GDScript and everything works fine, no need to call `close()` and setting the compression doesn't conflicts with anything

Here is a yt [video](https://youtu.be/Oz2PeCmZHcI) showcasing the error

Could https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/98358 possibly be related to this issue?

I tested with RC2 and the issue still exists.

Just tested this issue using **Godot stable mono 4.4.1** with **C#** in **Windows 10**, It seems that #102861 worked just fine, even when calling `host.Compress()`, now both `peer.Close()` and `peer.Dispose()` work correctly.
Note: setting `MultiplayerPeer = null` does not free the port immediately due to C# Garbage Collector limitations, so we need to explicitly call `peer.Close()` or `peer.Dispose()` on the host when closing the server.

#98358 Seems to be unrelated, since **this issue** is directly related to the C# Garbage Collector and I could not reproduce it using GDScript.
So Im just going to close this for now.
Thanks to everyone!
